summary.oneLiner: Record Q4 (45,000 KL, +14% volume, 3x industry) and first-ever INR 4,000 cr+ FY26 revenue confirm GULFOILLUB's structural share-gain story (No. 2 private brand), now layered with EV-charging (Tirex INR 100 cr) and data-centre-cooling optionality — but near-term margins face a sharp crude/base-oil spike from the Middle-East crisis, with mgmt defending a 12–14% EBITDA band via repeated price hikes.

thesis (one line): Record Q4 (45,000 KL, +14% volume, 3x industry) and first-ever INR 4,000 cr+ FY26 revenue confirm GULFOILLUB's structural share-gain story (No. 2 private brand), now layered with EV-charging (Tirex INR 100 cr) and data-centre-cooling optionality — but near-term margins face a sharp crude/base-oil spike from the Middle-East crisis, with mgmt defending a 12–14% EBITDA band via repeated price hikes.
scorecard (yoy): CALL-OUT — base-oil cost: Crude rallied from ~$65–70 (Feb) → $90+ (Mar), trending >$100 in current qtr, peaking ~$120 briefly; ~$95 "as we speak." Time-lag from crude→base-oil compressed from ~2 months to 1–2 weeks. ~50%+ base oil imported (Korea/Singapore refiners, feedstock from Middle East). Base oil inventory normally 45 days, raised to ~45–60 days for supply security; some refiners allocating at 80–90%.

One-offs: Some March-end demand pull-forward as customers/channel secured stock amid availability anxiety (mgmt insists Jan/Feb also double-digit, so underlying demand genuine). Rupee depreciation a headwind through FY26.
guidance (critical): Volume growth: Maintain 2–3x industry; market seen growing ~3–4% (~8–9% industry referenced by analyst). No upward revision — outlook unchanged, watching geopolitics. Target faster growth in low-share segments (PCMO <5%) and industrial (consistent double-digit). Distribution growth target 10–15% (urban + rural).
Margin band: Defend 12–14% EBITDA; aspiration to 14–16% if pricing stabilises. May trend toward lower band as realisations rise sharply (% optics). Cost levers + frequent price hikes to protect band.

EV / new-energy ramp: Tirex crossed INR 100 cr in FY26; aim to grow >30% bus-DC-charger share + expand AC chargers (MG Motors, VinFast). New Tirex plant operational Q3 FY27. EV fluids into "a number of OEMs." Data-centre cooling: 2 products (PAO synthetic + mineral) developed, material-compatibility tested, next step data-centre field testing — revenue timing not yet committable; volumes small.
demand: Broad-based, robust. Double-digit growth across PCMO, motorcycle/CV, agriculture (strong), OEM franchisee workshops (40+ OEMs across auto/industrial/construction), B2B industrial. Strong FY25 vehicle sales (2W, 4W, CV, tractors; rising EV penetration; GST help) aiding OEM/workshop business. Monsoon/July agri season seen supportive. March-end aided by stock-securing behaviour but underlying demand "robust"; customers willing to pay higher prices to ensure supply.
segment (auto / industrial / ev): Auto B2C (bazaar): Good share in motorcycle & diesel-engine-oil; growing mechanic engagement & distribution. PCMO low share = growth lever.
OEM/franchisee workshops: Key strength, 50–55+ OEMs, double-digit growth, leadership reinforced.
Industrial B2B: Consistent double-digit, strong trajectory.
AdBlue: Highest-ever volumes (40k KL qtr / 151k KL FY), +8%.

EV (Tirex): INR 100 cr milestone; 30–40% share of new bus DC chargers; AC chargers to MG Motors & VinFast; new customers/OEMs testing (construction, e-truck). Indra (UK) chargers being evaluated for India. EV fluids ramping with OEMs.
growth / optionality: EV charging (Tirex): core new-energy bet; ~1 charger per 4–5 EV buses; new plant Q3 FY27; AC + DC standardized for all vehicle types.
Indra (UK): global associate, leading UK AC-charger player; potential India entry.

Data-centre liquid-cooling fluids: market ~14–16 mn litres (small but fast-growing as air→liquid cooling shifts); 2 products ready, in compatibility/field-test phase; "good place to be," low-volume near-term.
Premiumisation: synthetic ester-based oils across categories; "Unlock 2.0" (accelerate, premiumize, transform) + digital/AI initiatives.
Market-share gains: structural, low-share segments (PCMO <5%) provide headroom.
margins & cost (base oil / crude): EBITDA 12–14% band under pressure from crude spike ($65→$120 peak, ~$95 now) and rupee depreciation. ~50%+ base oil imported; crude→base-oil lag compressed to 1–2 weeks. Multiple/successive price increases taken and planned (weekly/fortnightly cadence); realisations rising sharply per-litre but with some lag in realisation. Cost recalibration levers + ~45–60 day base-oil inventory cushion margins. A&P spend ~3–4% of revenue (calibrated by quarter). Priority explicitly: supply security first, pricing second.
capex: Chennai capacity expansion on track — on stream by Q3 FY27 (first).
Silvassa expansion — by Q4 FY27 (more civil work; started).
Tirex new plant — operational Q3 FY27; funded via equity + borrowings + working capital.
capital allocation (high dividend): Cash-generating; debt-light. Highest-ever FY26 dividend INR 51/share (INR 30 final + INR 21 interim) → payout up to ~72% (vs 30–40% three–four years ago). Payout raised pending larger M&A/EV investment opportunities. Increased Tirex stake 51%→65% (additional INR 38 cr). R&D for lubricants borne by global parent (off India P&L; large global team India-based).
risks: Base-oil / crude volatility: sharp spike + compressed lag squeezes margins; supply-chain risk if Middle-East crisis (Strait of Hormuz) prolongs — refiner allocations already at 80–90%.
EV-transition on ICE lubes: long-term structural risk to engine-oil demand (mitigated offensively via Tirex/EV fluids).
Competition: vs Castrol (analyst flagged GULFOILLUB operating margin ~half of Castrol's); pricing power gap closing only gradually; brand premium varies by category.
FX: rupee depreciation keeps input costs elevated.
Pull-forward: some March demand was stock-securing, possible Q1 normalisation.
mgmt tone: Confident, upbeat ("record quarter," "delighted"), but candid on margin/supply risk. Repeatedly stresses supply-security-over-pricing discipline and "margin management." Measured on data-centre/EV timing (refuses to commit revenue quarters). Will not comment on competitor specifics (Castrol procurement/premium).
non-obvious: Margin gap vs Castrol roughly 2x — closing only via volume operating leverage + brand-driven pricing power (slow).
AdBlue is a meaningful secondary volume stream (151k KL/yr) but lower-margin commodity.
Crude→base-oil pass-through lag collapsed to 1–2 weeks (vs historical ~2 months) — unusual, accelerates margin transmission both ways.
EV charging tied to bus electrification, which has under-delivered ("buses expected on road have not happened") — Tirex still won 30–40% of the smaller pie.
Brand built via cricket (MS Dhoni, Hardik Pandya, Smriti Mandhana, CSK 13+ yrs) despite global motorsports heritage — India-specific positioning.
R&D cost largely off India P&L (parent-funded) — structural margin/return support.
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): Record quarter — 45,000 KL (+14%, 3x industry), revenue +14%, EBITDA INR 135 cr (+8.5%, highest-ever). FY26: vol 1,68,000 KL (+10.5%), AdBlue 1,51,000 KL (+8%), revenue >INR 4,000 cr (first time), EBITDA INR 510 cr standalone / 514 cr consol. Dividend INR 51 (payout ~72%). Tirex INR 100 cr, stake →65%. Crude spike $65→$120 peak (~$95 now); 12–14% margin band defended via repeated price hikes. Chennai capex Q3 FY27 / Silvassa Q4 FY27 / Tirex plant Q3 FY27. Data-centre fluids in field-test phase.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
